![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081209/assets/8ddd8493662174e0ddaf9bdd63b0ec382f6bb25c9079f1a339b71400b8cf3860.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-6,6],$ is shown above. The areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $15$, $60$ and $9,$ respectively (from left to right). 

Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-6,6].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, we see that

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-15+60-9=36.
$$

So, applying the average value formula, we find that the average value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6-(-6)}\cdot (36) \\  & =\frac{36}{12} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
